statusText: Roughly three hours into the U.S. cash session, the Nasdaq-100 complex has extended Wednesday's soft-inflation tailwind into a firmer midday advance -- QQQ was reported up about 1.05% intraday, a step stronger than the ~0.2-0.3% seen earlier in the session -- while VIX stays compressed near 14.5 (down roughly 5% on the day) and Treasury yields continue easing on reinforced Fed-hold bets. Tail stays low with no observed failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure; Stress eases further from the post-open reading as the session continues to resolve calmly, though it stays in the moderate zone on the unresolved Hormuz standoff and tonight's pending Applied Materials earnings.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Reassess as the session either extends this gentle midday advance or fades into the close, and again around Applied Materials' after-close earnings call (~20:30 UTC) and tomorrow's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print; an upgrade to a higher Tail state requires observed persistent one-way structure with failed pullbacks, not the pending catalysts themselves.
headline: Nasdaq-100 extends its orderly midday advance -- QQQ up roughly 1% -- as VIX stays compressed near 14.5 and yields ease further; Tail remains low while Stress eases further ahead of tonight's Applied Materials earnings
body: Roughly three hours after the 13:30 UTC cash open, web reporting describes a firmer midday continuation of Wednesday's soft-inflation tailwind: Invesco QQQ Trust was reported up about 1.05% intraday, leading the S&P 500 and Dow, with Wall Street traders continuing to push bond yields lower on reinforced bets the Fed holds rates next month. NQ futures were again reported near 29,805.75, with an unchanged opening print (29,712.25) and an unchanged day range (29,668.25-30,001.75) versus the prior two runs' reads -- this repetition across three consecutive hourly checks strongly suggests the search-indexed NQ figure is a cached snapshot rather than a fresh tick, so it is treated as a low-confidence data point and not used to assert current range/structure; the fresher QQQ intraday percentage move is weighted instead as the best available proxy for today's price action. Even so, a gentle, one-sided ~1% grind without any reported failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure does not meet the bar for a Tail increase on its own. VIX was last reported near 14.55, down roughly 5% on the day, consistent with continued volatility compression. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD and WTI feeds again returned their most recent prints dated Aug 11 (10Y ~4.70%, 2Y ~4.22%, WTI ~$84.77/bbl), now four sessions stale; GLOBAL_QUOTE for QQQ again returned Aug 12's close (+0.73%) rather than an intraday read. This run's Alpha Vantage MARKET_STATUS call again returned Cloudflare 502 errors after one retry, so TOP_GAINERS_LOSERS was skipped this run to conserve the free-tier daily budget rather than risk a second consecutive failure; U.S. cash-session status is instead inferred from the current time (16:35 UTC, inside the 13:30-20:00 UTC session) and corroborating web reporting. Iran's Hormuz standoff remains unresolved -- a Basij Organisation commander reiterated Thursday that the strait is "under Iran's control and management" and that no vessel may transit without Iran's permission, directly rejecting Trump's "total control" claim from a day earlier -- with no fresh escalatory shock or transmission event identified, and no new Ukraine/Russia escalation was identified this run. Applied Materials still reports fiscal Q3 earnings after today's close with its call at 20:30 UTC (4:30pm ET); the stock was trading near $548 ahead of the print. Given the confirmed but still orderly, one-directional-but-shallow midday advance, Tail ticks up marginally to 16% (from 15%), still low, reflecting the slightly firmer and more persistent drift without crossing into pathological one-way territory. Stress eases further to 34% as the session continues to resolve without incident and VIX extends its compression, moving toward the lower end of the moderate zone while the unresolved Hormuz backdrop and the pending Applied Materials print keep it out of the low band. Confidence eases to 50%, reflecting the Alpha Vantage Treasury/oil feeds growing more stale (now four sessions), a QQQ quote still anchored to yesterday's close, a second consecutive MARKET_STATUS failure, and an NQ futures read that now appears unchanged across three consecutive hourly checks, offset by fresher web corroboration of today's QQQ intraday move, VIX level, and the Hormuz update.

outlookSummary: The next 24 hours stay tradable under the Tail rule. Forecast Tail holds in the mid-teens throughout the window, with Stress easing further into the afternoon before building toward tonight's 20:00 UTC close and Applied Materials earnings reaction (~20:30-21:00 UTC), and once more heading into tomorrow's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print. None of these bumps cross the WATCH threshold on this run's evidence; an upgrade requires observed post-catalyst continuation with failed retracements, not the catalyst itself or a lack of confirming data.

forecastDetail.comment: Roughly three hours into the cash session, the confirmed move firms modestly (QQQ intraday +~1.05%) while still lacking any observed failed-pullback or repeated-extension structure; VIX near 14.5 shows no stress build, so Tail holds near its recent low level.

Approaching the mid-afternoon lull, Stress continues easing as the session resolves calmly without incident; the pending Applied Materials earnings call (20:30 UTC) has not yet begun to move implied volatility.

Into the final cash-session hour, dispersion ahead of Applied Materials' after-close report and the approaching 20:00 UTC close begins to lift Stress modestly; Tail stays contained absent observed one-way continuation.

The 19:00-20:00 UTC window covers the cash close and the run-up to Applied Materials' 20:30 UTC earnings call; Stress rises on event proximity and potential thin-liquidity whipsaw, not on any asserted pre-print price structure.

Applied Materials' post-earnings reaction window (~20:30-21:00 UTC) carries the session's largest single-name catalyst; Stress peaks here on realistic surprise-magnitude risk while Tail requires an observed, persistent post-print trend to move materially.

As the initial earnings reaction fades into the late U.S. evening, Stress begins retreating from its peak while dominant mode stays event/whipsaw pending confirmation that any post-AMAT move either extends or mean-reverts.
